clue.text: Item of military dress worn mostly flush

parts.note: worn as in threadbare, bald, with the nap or tread rubbed away

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: flush means having plenty of money, rich

explanation.surface: Some piece of army uniform that has been worn so much it has almost been wiped clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldric is a belt worn over one shoulder to carry a sword, part of military costume.

clue.text: Art of growing up among Asia's nobility

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
among says the answer sits within the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: An art of cultivation flourishes among the Asian aristocracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' belongs to the wordplay: the answer runs backwards inside ASIAS NOBility.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese art of cultivating miniature trees in pots.

clue.text: Harass healers to despair

indicators.note: to harass is to disturb or agitate, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Pestering doctors drives them to despair.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is to become discouraged, to give up hope.

clue.text: Fabric drawers with sides having split

indicators.note: having split means left; with the sides gone, the outer letters of the word are dropped

parts.note: crayons are things you draw with, drawers in a cryptic sense

explanation.surface: Fabric chest of drawers whose sides have come apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawers' suggests underwear or furniture, but means things that draw: crayons.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic textile made from regenerated cellulose.

clue.text: Find fault with account linked to satellite dish

parts.note: to carp is to find fault, to complain
Io is a moon of Jupiter, a satellite

explanation.surface: A complaint about a bill for installing a satellite dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'satellite dish' looks like one item, but the satellite is a moon and the dish is food.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpaccio is an Italian dish of thinly sliced raw beef or fish.

clue.text: Monopolise department on small Scottish plant

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the department letter comes after the Scottish word

parts.note: to hog something is to monopolise it
wee is the Scottish word for small

explanation.surface: Someone hogs a whole department, sitting on a tiny Scottish plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogweed is a tall wild umbellifer, a weed of verges and riverbanks.

clue.text: God cheated over empty eulogies

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the word for cheated above the rest

parts.note: to be had is to be cheated or conned

indicators.note: empty means the inner letters are removed, leaving the outside

explanation.surface: A god was deceived by hollow praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the Greek god of the underworld, brother of Zeus.

clue.text: Order music

parts.note: the clue reads as an instruction to arrange or request music, but means music sung by a religious order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a verb; it is a monastic order, whose plainsong is named after Pope Gregory.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregorian chant is the plainsong of the Western church, sung by monks in religious communities.

clue.text: Praise former partner over large amount raised

indicators.note: over puts the former partner above the rest in this down entry

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a lot is a large amount

explanation.surface: Someone praises an ex who has raised a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically, to laud.

clue.text: Mock the German papers on centre of shelf

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the papers above the next piece

parts.note: der is a German word for the
ID, identification, is a person's papers

indicators.note: centre of means the middle letter of shelf

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at German newspapers on the middle of a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to ridicule or scorn, to make fun of.

clue.text: Intrusive binary responses one sent back

parts.note: the two possible answers to a yes/no question; here the first taken is no

indicators.note: sent back means the word for the second response is written backwards

parts.note: one of those binary responses, the other one: yes

explanation.surface: A survey of only yes-or-no questions feels intrusive, so someone returns one form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binary responses' is the pair of answers to a closed question, and both are used: the negative as it stands, the positive written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nosey pries into others' affairs, which is an intrusive way to behave.

clue.text: Irish pet maybe embarrassed me

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red in the face
in a crossword, 'me' is the compiler, the setter

explanation.surface: Someone is embarrassed when their Irish pet does something in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is a crossword convention: the person speaking in the clue is the compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: The red setter is an Irish breed of gun dog, often kept as a family pet; 'maybe' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Greeks struggling in heat since about noon

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of 'in heat' are thrown into disorder
about means the word for since goes around the noon letter

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it was late'

explanation.surface: Some Greeks have been toiling in the heat ever since around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Athenians are citizens of Athens, the Greek capital, so they are Greek people.

clue.text: Baffled fellow leaving worse for wear

indicators.note: leaving means the fellow letter departs from the word for baffled

parts.note: to foil a plan is to baffle it, so baffled gives foiled

explanation.surface: A confused man walks out of the room looking rather the worse for wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is slang for drunk, and a drunk person is the worse for wear.

clue.text: Outbreak is equally reckless

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sudden outbreak, of spots or of events
second meaning: acting without thought, reckless

explanation.surface: An epidemic is just as reckless as people's behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is equally' only links the two meanings: the word for an outbreak is the same as the word for reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense, a spate or eruption of spots, and an adjective sense, hasty and imprudent, share one spelling.

clue.text: Clown discovered King and Queen at home

indicators.note: discovered means the cover, the outer letters, is taken off

parts.note: Charles, King of the UK
in means at home

explanation.surface: A clown spotted the King and Queen relaxing at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' looks like 'found' but means stripped of its covering letters, so CHARLES becomes HARLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin is the masked comic servant of commedia dell'arte, a clown figure in pantomime.

clue.text: Sheep herder originally re-dug yonder pit

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog, bred to herd sheep

indicators.note: originally means the start of each of the next two words is taken

explanation.surface: A sheepdog has been digging over the ground and found a pit yonder.
explanation.definitionFit: A colliery is a coal mine, and a mine is often called a pit.

clue.text: Lost in details written in Ovid's language

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have wandered astray and are muddled

explanation.surface: Something got lost in the fine detail of a Latin text.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was a Roman poet writing in Latin; to latinise is to render into Latin.

clue.text: Appear again outside of refuge with beach dude?

indicators.note: outside of means the outer letters of refuge

parts.note: a surf ace is an expert surfer, a dude on the beach; the question mark flags the made-up phrase

explanation.surface: A cool surfer reappears at a shelter on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: To resurface is to come back up to the surface, or to show up again after an absence.

clue.text: Get going with best-performing ticket seller

parts.note: the best performer is the star
a tout sells tickets, often unofficially at a mark-up

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to work with the most successful ticket seller.
explanation.definitionFit: To start out is to begin a journey or a career, to set off.

clue.text: Administration that launches 9 perhaps endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: 9 across is nosey; nasal means of the nose, so it is a nose-y word, 'perhaps' flagging the loose sense

explanation.surface: Some agency sends rockets up, possibly the one in 9.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference reads as a launch of answer 9; in fact 'nosey' is taken literally as 'of the nose', which is nasal.
explanation.definitionFit: NASA is the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration, which launches spacecraft.

clue.text: Mark in Jersey possibly missing new film

indicators.note: missing means the new letter is taken out
in means the mark letter goes inside the word for cow-like

parts.note: a Jersey is a breed of cow, so bovine; 'possibly' marks the example
M is short for mark, as in the German currency

explanation.surface: A mark in a Jersey cow's ear, perhaps, is missing in a new film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' suggests the island or a jumper; here it is the dairy cow breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A B-movie is a low-budget film, originally the lesser half of a double bill.

clue.text: Often subjects set in first year initially get harder

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each preceding word

explanation.surface: School subjects set in the first year often get harder.
explanation.definitionFit: To ossify is to turn into bone, hence to harden or become rigid.

clue.text: Roughly trim back of ornate tile for bishop

indicators.note: roughly suggests the letters of trim are rearranged in a rough, inexact way
back of means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A tiler roughly trims the back of a decorative tile for a bishop's palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tile' is old slang for a hat, so a bishop's tile is his tall hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre is the tall pointed headdress worn by a bishop, and tile is slang for hat.

clue.text: Fish snare upset children

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: a net is a snare

explanation.surface: Children upset when a fishing trap is knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: Tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Very busy certainly with head-to-toe treatments

parts.note: manic means frantically busy

indicators.note: head-to-toe means the first letter of the word for certainly goes to its end

parts.note: sure means certainly, as in 'sure, I will'

explanation.surface: A frantic beauty salon offers full head-to-toe treatments, for certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head-to-toe' looks like part of the definition, but it moves the S of SURE to the end, giving URES.
explanation.definitionFit: Manicures are cosmetic care of the hands and nails, a kind of beauty treatment.

clue.text: Resources tight before middle of recession

indicators.note: before puts the word for tight ahead of the letter from recession

parts.note: tight means stingy, mean

indicators.note: the middle letter of recession

explanation.surface: Money is tight ahead of the middle of a recession.
explanation.definitionFit: Means are financial resources, as in 'living within your means'.

clue.text: See 6
Local wine and half a curry university covers

parts.note: the first half of vindaloo, a hot curry
covers as in covers the cost, pays

explanation.surface: Students order local wine and a curry, and the university pays the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Vin de pays is French for 'country wine', a local wine from a defined region.

clue.text: Sailor regularly at chic counters

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A sailor turns up regularly at stylish bars and counters.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads for counting; abaci are counting devices, so counters.

clue.text: Spiny thing moved inches across back of bayou

indicators.note: across means the shuffled letters stretch across, surrounding the bayou letter
moved means the letters of inches are shifted into a new order
back of means the last letter of bayou

explanation.surface: A prickly creature shuffles a few inches across the far side of a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Echinus is the zoological name for the sea urchin, a creature covered in spines.

clue.text: Hesitant when switching articles in journal

indicators.note: switching means one article in the word for journal is exchanged for another

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal
a and the are the two English articles; the indefinite one is swapped for the definite

explanation.surface: Someone dithers over which articles to use when writing up a journal.
explanation.walkthrough: The indefinite article A in DIARY is switched for the definite article THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dithery describes someone who wavers and cannot make up their mind, so hesitant.
